item.title: Economist Says 6% Growth Target Becomes Ever More Elusive
item.description: Jakarta. International Economic Association Secretary General Lili Yan Ing has urged the government to take a more measured and consistent approach in setting its economic growth targets, cautioning that overly ambitious figures could weaken policy credibility in the eyes of the market. Speaking to B-Universe on Wednesday, Lili said the widely cited 6% growth target does not fully reflect current economic conditions and risks creating uncertainty if it is not supported by realistic assumptions.

item.title: BNI Cleans Up Flood-Hit Darul Aman Mosque
item.description: Jakarta. State-run bank BNI continues to launch recovery initiatives in the flood-hit West Sumatra. This time, the bank has helped clear mud and flood debris at the Darul Aman Mosque in Jorong Toboh, Nagari Malalak. The initiative enables the local people to comfortably pray at the mosque. BNI's post-disaster recovery focuses on public facilities that are strategically important to the community's social and religious life. item.title: Jakarta Market Defies Wall Street and Asia Sell-Off, Opens Firmly Higher
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia’s benchmark Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) continued its upward momentum at Thursday’s open, defying overnight declines on Wall Street and a mostly weaker Asia-Pacific session. JCI opened higher on Thursday, rising to 9,072 in early trade, moving within a range of 9,047 to 9,081. item.title: Antam Gold Extends Record Rally for Fourth Day on Global Turmoil
item.description: Jakarta. Gold prices in Indonesia extended their rally on Thursday, with Antam bullion hitting a fresh all-time high for the fourth consecutive day, tracking record gains in global markets amid rising geopolitical and economic uncertainty. Antam’s one-gram gold bar climbed Rp 10,000 to Rp 2,675,000 ($158.57) per gram on Thursday, according to Logam Mulia data. item.title: Japan and the Philippines Sign a New Defense Pact Allowing Tax-Free Ammunition Supplies
item.description: Manila. item.title: Indonesia’s External Debt Stands at $423.8 Billion in November
item.description: Jakarta.
